**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Fix broken quoting in rate-limit check command**

When the `Checking Rate Limit Status` snippet is copied into a shell, the `python3 -c "..."` string contains unescaped `"` characters in `r["remaining"]`/`r["limit"]`, so the inner key quotes are stripped before Python evaluates the f-string. This causes a runtime `NameError` instead of printing quota data, making the documented command unusable for the exact workflow this section introduces.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Restore labels on force and moment balance equations**

This change removes the `{#eq-force_balance}` and `{#eq-moment_balance}` anchors from the Euler balance equations, but later text still references `@eq-force_balance` (and previously referenced the moment equation). In Quarto output this leaves unresolved cross-references, so readers lose clickable equation targets and see broken numbering for core derivation steps.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Cite the moment-balance equation in Step 5**

Step 5 now says `\sum \mathbf{M}_{\text{COM}}` is known from `@eq-force_balance`, but that quantity comes from the moment-balance equation, not the force-balance equation. Even if labels are restored, this reference points to the wrong relation and makes the derivation logically inconsistent for readers following the inverse-dynamics steps.

comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve relative history links when sanitizing URLs**

Using `parsed.href` here rewrites stored history entries to be rooted at the site origin, but `updateHistorySidebar` stores only the basename (`window.location.pathname.split('/').pop()` / `urlFromPath`). For pages under subdirectories (for example `/articles/...` or `/models/...`), an entry like `theory-part1.html` now becomes `https://<host>/theory-part1.html`, dropping its directory and leading to broken navigation (often 404) when users click recent-history links. This regression is introduced by replacing the original relative `item.url` assignment with origin-normalized `parsed.href`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
